assumptions: Finite-dimensional real Hilbert/Borel space E; rank zero included as an explicit authored extension.
Any actual probability measure μ, any η>0 and any globally C1 real observer f with compact support; no centering or finite-moment/input-density premise.
R_y and S_y are exactly the displayed quadratic tilt and affine reflected pushforward at every y. The source-volume Gibbs density identity is a separate downstream adapter.
All observer/derivative bounds, measurability, genuine L1, dominated differentiation, continuous integrated derivative and positive normalization are internal outputs, not convenience binders.
units.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space equipped with its Borel measurable structure, including rank zero. Let μ be any probability measure, η>0, and f:E→ℝ a globally C1 function with compact support. For every y∈E define R_y=μ.tilted(x↦−‖x−y‖²/(2η)) and S_y=(x↦2x−y)_#R_y. Then the exact function m(y)=∫f(u)S_y(du) is globally C1. These are the specified everywhere-defined posterior and reflection laws; no arbitrary AE conditional version is substituted. Moment, input density, domination, normalization, derivative-continuity and closed-gradient certificates are not premises. This is explicitly attributed authored analytic background for the paper’s normalized-density differentiation with its Gibbs input and smooth compact tests.

steps.title: Bound the compact observer and its actual derivative
steps.text: C1 gives continuous f and continuous Frechet derivative. Compact support of f also gives compact support of its derivative. Compactness therefore supplies finite global bounds Mf and Md. Introduce the literal Gaussian weight K, weighted observer F and normalizing integral Z; the probability measure makes every constant bound integrable.

steps.title: Keep both genuine parameter derivatives and a uniform Gaussian bound
steps.text: The weight derivative is K′=−(K/η)〈y−x,·〉. The reflection parameter derivative is −Id, giving −Df(2x−y). The product rule retains both terms. The exponential estimate K‖y−x‖²≤2η and r≤1+r² give a uniform bound on K′; combine it with compact observer bounds. No input moment is used.

steps.title: Differentiate the actual weighted numerator under the integral
steps.text: Continuity in x gives precise AEStrong measurability for F and its actual Frechet derivative G. The observer bound proves genuine L1 of F. The uniform derivative bound is integrable under μ. Apply the pinned global dominated Frechet differentiation theorem on the whole parameter space, deriving the derivative of N from actual G.
steps.formula: N(y)=\int F(y,x)\mu(dx),\quad DN(y)=\int D_yF(y,x)\mu(dx),\quad F(y,\cdot)\in L^1(\mu),\quad\|D_yF\|\le M_d+M_f(1+2\eta)/\eta\in L^1(\mu).

steps.title: Prove continuous derivative, hence C1 numerator
steps.text: For every fixed x, G(y,x) is continuous in y because f and its derivative are continuous and the Gaussian/affine factors are continuous. The same global bound gives dominated continuity of the CLM-valued integral D(y). The genuine derivative identity and continuous D produce C1 N.
steps.formula: D(y)=\int G(y,x)\mu(dx)\in C^0(E,E\to\mathbb R),\qquad DN=D,\qquad N\in C^1(E).

steps.title: Identify the literal every-y normalized mean before quotient calculus
steps.text: Reuse the existing Gaussian-convolution positive C2 normalizer. Positivity of its exact density prefactor times Z makes Z nonzero everywhere. Internally show Gaussian likelihood L1, so the actual tilt is a probability; bounded f then yields posterior L1 and mapped-observer L1 before using integral_map. The actual integral_tilted identity and norm symmetry identify exactly the same mean N/Z at every y. C1 numerator and positive C2 denominator conclude C1 of this literal mean.
steps.formula: Z(y)=\int K(y,x)\mu(dx)>0,\quad Z\in C^2,\quad \int f\,dS_y=\int f(2x-y)\,dR_y=\frac{N(y)}{Z(y)},\quad m=N/Z\in C^1.

steps.text: The existing macroscopic-energy theorem produces probability of the source Gibbs μ under unchanged curvature and step bounds. The existing GaussianConditionalKernel constructs a true Markov conditional R for the same augmentation J and identifies its literal fiber at every y, so the new theorem applies to its reflected mean. This does not assert equality to the separate source-volume S density. The rank-zero standard Gaussian posterior/reflection yields the noncentered observer1 with real mean1 and actual Frechet derivative0.
steps.formula: \mu=dx.\operatorname{tilted}(-V),\quad J=\operatorname{law}(X,X+\sqrt\eta G),\quad R_y=\mu.\operatorname{tilted}(-\|x-y\|^2/(2\eta))\ \forall y;\qquad\dim E=0,\ f=1:\ m\equiv1,\ Dm\equiv0.
